  printf 'x' >> "$tmpdir/sample_R1.check-demo.fastq.gz"
  expected=$(awk '$2 == "sample_R1.fastq.gz" {print $1}' SHA256SUMS)

  • QC shifts: verify metric units, group sizes, and metadata; a batch shift can arise from technical or design differences, but a plot alone cannot identify its cause.

Smoke-test the saved files

After running the aggregation block, this checks the documented output files for a gene column, non-negative integer counts, and sample columns aligned to the sample sheet. It does not fit a model or report differential-expression results.

counts_file <- readr::read_csv(
  "output/pseudobulk/cd4_counts.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
samples_file <- readr::read_csv(
  "output/pseudobulk/sample_metadata.csv",
  col_types = readr::cols(
    sample_id = readr::col_character(),
    .default = readr::col_guess()
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

stopifnot(
  "gene" %in% names(counts_file),
  all(c("sample", "sample_id", "condition") %in% names(samples_file))
)

count_samples <- names(counts_file)[names(counts_file) != "gene"]
stopifnot(identical(count_samples, samples_file$sample_id))

count_values <- as.matrix(counts_file[count_samples])
stopifnot(
  all(is.finite(count_values)),
  all(count_values >= 0),
  all(abs(count_values - round(count_values)) < 1e-8)
)

If a check fails, inspect the saved files and sample order before modeling. Passing checks establish file structure only; they do not verify the source assay, study design, or biological validity.

Fit DESeq2 and make the contrast explicit

Choose design terms from the study design before looking at outcomes. Do not put both condition and a perfectly confounded batch term into a model and expect it to identify their separate effects.

# Illustrative low-count prefilter; review for your cohort and design.
keep_gene <- rowSums(pb) >= 10
if (!any(keep_gene)) stop("No genes pass the illustrative count filter")

For a diploid, high-quality biallelic germline call, heterozygous and homozygous-alternate genotypes often have allele fractions near 0.5 and 1, respectively. A histogram is descriptive, not a genotype caller: depth, allele balance, ploidy, mapping/base quality, contamination, and capture bias affect the values.
